title: I Hear the Voice of Woe
description: I Hear the Voice of Woe in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: William Enfield wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 823 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Forgiveness”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: I hear the voice of woe! I hear a broth-er's sigh! Then let my heart with pi-ty flow, With tears of love, my eye.

lines: I hear the voice of woe!
Then let my heart with pity flow,
With tears of love, my eye.
Then let my spring its stream supply,
Can hope bear high my prayer,
Up to thy throne, my God, my King,

licence: Public domain: William Enfield died in 1797.
credits: Words by William Enfield (1741–1797), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
